key_findings.finding: card1=1976 carries a matured (label-lagged) fraud rate of 18.94%, ~5.4x the ~3.5% base rate, over 867 prior transactions — a genuine high-risk entity, not noise.

The card1+email combination shows an even higher matured fraud rate of 34.05%, and this exact rule (R_PRIOR_FRAUD_CARD1_EMAIL) fired with 19.11% historical fraud, 5.4x lift over 16,801 supporting cases.
card1=1976 has a maximal gang_score of 1.0 with extreme device fan-out (101 devices), plus 12 addr1 and 13 email fan-out — a classic gang/entity-abuse topology.
Transaction-level attributes (ProductCD=C at 11.4% fraud, card6=credit, DeviceType=desktop) are moderately elevated risk categories, consistent with the GBDT score direction.

CONFLICT with GBDT p=0.8242: all 4 structurally-similar retrieved cases sharing this exact fingerprint (card1=1976, ProductCD=C, visa/credit, gmail, $100-300 amt) were human-cleared false positives — including one at model score 0.65. This suggests this specific pattern is prone to false positives despite the entity's overall fraud history.
The email domain itself (gmail.com, 4.4% fraud) is near base rate and NOT a driver; the risk concentrates in the card1 entity, not the transaction's generic attributes.
card1+addr1 has zero prior history (new entity-address pairing), triggering R_NEW_ENTITY (7.78% fraud), though addr1 field is missing in the snapshot.

gang_association.rationale: card1=1976 shows a maximal gang_score (1.0), extreme device fan-out (101 devices across 867 txns), and matured fraud rates of 18.94% (card1) / 34.05% (card1+email) — a strong, label-confirmed team/entity-abuse pattern. The specific transaction may or may not itself be fraudulent (similar cases were cleared), but the underlying entity is a confirmed high-risk hub warranting entity-level action.

report.disposition_rationale: Under the cost framework, entity-level gang evidence (matured 18.94–34.05% fraud rate + gang_score 1.0 + fan-out 101) makes freezing/investigating card1=1976 highly cost-effective even at $179.83, since it can halt batch fraud. A blunt decline is disfavored because 4 identical-fingerprint cases were human-cleared false positives (including one at 0.65) — so this individual txn's fraud status is uncertain despite the high entity risk. Escalation ($40) routes to a team that can act on the entity while a human adjudicates this specific charge.
report.summary: Transaction 3537316 ($179.83, ProductCD=C, visa/credit, gmail, desktop) sits on card1=1976, a confirmed high-risk entity: matured fraud rate 18.94% (34.05% with email), gang_score 1.0, and device fan-out of 101 across 867 prior transactions — strongly corroborating the GBDT score's direction at the entity level. However, this exact transaction fingerprint has a track record of human-cleared false positives: all 4 similar retrieved cases (same card1, ProductCD, card type, email, amount band) were washed clean, one even at model score 0.65. This is a genuine conflict — the entity is dangerous, but this specific pattern over-triggers. Rather than a blunt decline, I recommend escalate: the gang/entity evidence justifies entity-level action against card1=1976, while a human adjudicates whether this individual charge is a true positive or another look-alike false positive.
